text:
mohit: Heads up — after yesterday's proxy rollout we're seeing client cert fields drop from backend audit logs in eu-west. Noticed it on a few user-facing routes.
anya: saw that in the dashboards too. is the proxy terminating mTLS and re-establishing plain TLS to the services?
sam: yep proxy does TLS termination -> mTLS to backend is disabled for performance in the new config. we only forward an X-Forwarded-Client-Cert header now.
kai: that explains it. but from a compliance perspective we need original client cert identity in immutable audit logs (CN + SAN + serial). header forwarding isn't acceptable unless signed and validated.
mohit: agreed. main ask from compliance: no loss of client cert provenance, and RBAC audits should be able to map requests to cert subjects.
anya: quick question — where are audit logs currently ingested? splunk? we need to know if the header is being stripped by the collector.
sam: logs go to splunk via forwarder on each service. right now the proxy writes its own access log with client cert info in a different schema. backends log the header as plain text but it's not canonical.
kai: this is a couple of problems: 1) provenance: proxy log vs backend log mismatch 2) tampering: headers can be spoofed 3) KMS signing: we should sign the proxy-to-backend handoff or use mTLS all the way.
mohit: can we do short-term mitigation: add a signed header from proxy that includes cert fingerprint and timestamp? example: X-Client-Cert-Sig: base64( sign_kms("cn=foo;serial=...;ts=..."))
sam: doable. proxy can call internal KMS-sign endpoint to attach an HMAC/sig. but that'll need KMS permissions (rbac) for the proxy role across regions.
anya: who owns the KMS roles for these proxies? i remember apac proxies run under a different service account.
kai: I own EU proxies, but APAC is under infra-sre. we need a short RACI: grant kms:Sign to proxy-role, but only for a per-region key with strict key policy and audit logging enabled.
sec-rotator-bot: scheduled key policy review job ran 2026-03-19T04:12Z. eu-west-kms-key: last rotation 2026-02-10, rotation_window=30d. recent grants: proxy-role-eu:Grant, service-account-infra:Grant.
mohit: thanks bot. kai / sam — can you prototype the signed-header approach and a verification library for backends? throw a small verifier in our shared middleware. should verify signature against region-specific KMS public key and reject mismatches.
sam: will do. prototype timeline: today -> basic sign + verify; tomorrow -> add replay protection (nonce/timestamp). code snippet i'll try:
```
# proxy side pseudo
payload = f"cn={cert.subject};serial={cert.serial};ts={now.isoformat()}"
sig = kms.sign(key=region_key, payload=payload)
req.headers['X-Client-Cert'] = payload
req.headers['X-Client-Cert-Sig'] = base64url(sig)
```

kai: backend verifier pseudocode:
```
if not verify_kms_signature(region_key, req.headers['X-Client-Cert'], req.headers['X-Client-Cert-Sig']):
  reject(401)
# then parse payload, add to audit event canonical_subject = payload.cn
```

anya: RBAC question: if we allow the proxy to sign, we need to ensure that downstream services cannot effectively elevate privileges by forging additional attributes. audit pipeline should only take subject from signed payload and map to existing RBAC principal.
mohit: good call. we should ignore any claim headers set by clients and only trust the signed one. update the RBAC middleware to prefer the verified certificate subject and drop conflicting headers.
sam: also found a vuln/triage note: some older proxies haven't had retry-without-header protection and will re-add headers on 502 retries. i'll add a guard to not reattach cert headers on retries.
kai: for long term — we should evaluate enabling mTLS passthrough mode for sensitive routes (payments, admin APIs) so provenance is preserved without relying on signed headers. that has perf cost but simpler trust model.
anya: action items: 1) sam prototype signed header + middleware verifier (ETA EOD) 2) kai coordinate KMS grants in eu/apac + update key policies (ETA 2 days) 3) mohit update compliance doc and list critical routes for passthrough (ETA 1 day) 4) sam add retry-guard and tests (ETA tomorrow) 5) anya run an audit to ensure Splunk parsers ingest proxy logs and signed headers correctly (ETA 2 days).
mohit: i'll own rollout gating: we only enable header-based acceptance after signed verification is in place and we've done a 48h canary in eu-west.
sec-rotator-bot: canary deploy of proxy v2 to eu-west started 2026-03-19T06:30Z. health=green.
sam: i'll open a short PR with middleware + unit tests and link it here in a few hours.
kai: FYI also pinged infra-sre for APAC KMS cross-account grant; they acknowledged.
anya: thanks all. once sam posts PR i'll validate splunk pipeline and add parser mapping. if anything looks off i'll flag here. :thumbsup:
mohit: thanks team. this keeps us compliant and avoids silent cert drops.
